title: Hemavata: “Is he without desire for sensual pleasures? Is his mind undisturbed? Has he overcome all delusion? Does he truly have eyes for all things?”…
content:
Hemavata:
“Is he without desire for sensual pleasures?
Is his mind undisturbed?
Has he overcome all delusion?
Does he truly have eyes for all things?”

Sātāgira:
“He has no desire for sensual pleasures,
His mind is undisturbed,
He has overcome all delusion —
The Buddha truly has eyes for all things.”

title: “Monks, suppose there is a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and…
content: “Monks, suppose there is a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. Someone says to him: ‘Good man, this bitter gourd is mixed with poison. If you wish, eat it. While eating, you will not find delight in its color, smell, or taste. After eating, you may meet death or deadly suffering.’ That man might eat it without reflection, without refusal. While eating, he does not find delight in its color, smell, or taste. After eating, he meets death or deadly suffering. Monks, I say that this course of practice is like that simile — namely, a course of practice that is painful in the present and also has painful results in the future.”

title: “Monks, what is clinging and worry? Here, monks, an untaught ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained…
content: “Monks, what is clinging and worry? Here, monks, an untaught ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained in the noble Dhamma, not seeing the true persons, not skilled in the true Dhamma, not trained in the true Dhamma, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. For him, that form changes and alters. Because of the change and alteration of form, his consciousness follows that change in form. Worrying states arise from that consciousness following the change in form, invading his mind and remaining. Because his mind is invaded, he is terrified, distressed, and full of longing and worry.”

title: “Then I, after some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the…
content: “Then I, after some time, having known as they actually are the origination, the passing away, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in the case of sensual pleasures, abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, removed the fever for sensual pleasures, and dwelt with craving cut off, with mind inwardly peaceful. Then I saw other beings who had not abandoned lust for sensual pleasures being consumed by craving for sensual pleasures, being burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures. I did not envy them, nor did I delight in that. Why is that? Because, Māgandiya, there is this pleasure and rapture, apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome states, and having attained the heavenly pleasure, I dwell delighting in that. I do not envy what is inferior, nor do I delight in that.”

title: “Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms,…
content: “Householder, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, depending on them, consciousness arises with clinging to them. Householder, a monk who has clinging does not attain complete Nibbāna … Households, there are tastes cognizable by the tongue … Householder, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — because he delights, praises, and dwells with lust, depending on them, consciousness arises with clinging to them. Having clinging, householder, that monk does not attain Nibbāna. This, householder, is the cause, this is the reason why some beings here and now do not attain complete Nibbāna.”

title: “Here, monks, the third kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins … have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we make a…
content: “Here, monks, the third kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘Those first ascetics and brahmins … have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we make a hiding place near the bait cast by Māra and the world’s offerings. Having made a hiding place, without entering, without indulging, we will eat the bait and the world’s offerings. By not entering, not indulging, we will not become infatuated; not infatuated, we will not become heedless; not heedless, we will not become subject to Māra’s will among that bait and offerings.’ These ascetics and brahmins make a hiding place near the bait and offerings. Having done so, without entering, without indulging, they eat the bait and offerings. Not entering, not indulging, they do not become infatuated; not infatuated, they do not become heedless; not heedless, they do not become subject to Māra’s will. But then they have such wrong views as: ‘The world is eternal; the world is not eternal; the world is finite; the world is infinite …’ Thus, monks, these third ascetics and brahmins have not escaped Māra’s power.”

title: - What gives birth to a person? What always runs about? What undergoes rebirth? What does a person rely on? - Craving gives birth to…
content:
- What gives birth to a person?
What always runs about?
What undergoes rebirth?
What does a person rely on?
- Craving gives birth to a person,
The mind itself always runs about,
Beings undergo rebirth,
Kamma is what a person relies on.

title: “Great king, there are three things in the world which, when they arise, lead to harm, suffering, and discomfort. What three? Great king, greed is…
content:
“Great king, there are three things in the world which, when they arise, lead to harm, suffering, and discomfort. What three? Great king, greed is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. Great king, hatred is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. Great king, delusion is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. These three things in the world, when they arise, bring harm, suffering, and discomfort.

Greed, hatred, delusion — these three,
Are evil minds for a person,
They damage one’s own self,
They produce one’s own self,
Like the rind and core of a tree,
Producing its own fruit.”

title: Bemused by wealth and sensual pleasures, People are greedy and deluded, In the midst of sensual pleasures, Without clear awareness, They are overly intoxicated, Like…
content:
Bemused by wealth and sensual pleasures,
People are greedy and deluded,
In the midst of sensual pleasures,
Without clear awareness,
They are overly intoxicated,
Like a fish unaware of the trap set —
Later they suffer,
Experiencing the results of evil deeds.

title: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition for the purification of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively happiness, immersed in happiness, accompanied…
content: “What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition for the purification of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively happiness, immersed in happiness, accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by suffering, beings would not become disenchanted with form. But because form is suffering, Mahāli, immersed in suffering, accompanied by suffering, not accompanied by happiness, beings become disenchanted with form. Through disenchantment, they become dispassionate; through dispassion, they are liberated. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the purification of beings. Such being the cause, such being the condition, beings are purified. If feeling … perception … formations … if consciousness were exclusively happiness … beings would not become disenchanted with consciousness. But because consciousness is suffering … beings become disenchanted with consciousness … and are liberated. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the purification of beings.”
